p1.en: To start dealing with the serious or important matter at hand.
p1.ex1: She assessed her CV and decided to get down to business before the interview.
p1.ex2: Soft skills matter, but eventually you have to get down to business and collaborate.
p1.example: After the introduction, the manager said it was time to get down to business.

p2.en: A person whose job is to manage financial records and accounts.
p2.ex1: She collaborated with the accountant to manage the soft skills training budget.
p2.ex2: Her CV listed accountant experience alongside collaboration and management skills.
p2.example: The accountant assessed the company's finances before it went bankrupt.

p2.en: The ability to adjust to new conditions or situations.
p2.ex1: The manager assessed adaptability alongside originality and collaboration in the CV.
p2.ex2: Her adaptability helped the team avoid going bankrupt during the difficult period.
p2.example: Adaptability is one of the most valued soft skills when running a business.

p2.en: A reason given to support or oppose something; or a disagreement.
p2.ex1: She consulted the management team and assessed each argument about running a business.
p2.ex2: Collaboration reduces workplace argument and improves productivity and soft skills.
p2.example: The employee made a strong argument for improving the dress code policy.

p2.en: To evaluate or judge the nature, quality, or ability of something.
p2.ex1: She assessed the argument about the dress code before consulting the employee.
p2.ex2: Assessing collaboration and teamwork helps management avoid the business going bankrupt.
p2.example: The manager assessed each CV for soft skills, adaptability and originality.

p2.en: A person who helps someone else with their work.
p2.ex1: She was hired as an assistant after her CV demonstrated collaboration and soft skills.
p2.ex2: The assistant assessed rejection letters alongside the management team.
p2.example: The assistant managed the dress code documents and consulted the accountant.

p2.en: To work together with others to achieve a goal.
p2.ex1: Management assessed how well employees could collaborate under the dress code policy.
p2.ex2: Collaboration and adaptability are the soft skills most valued when running a business.
p2.example: She collaborated with the accountant and assistant to run the business efficiently.

p2.en: The action of working with someone to produce something.
p2.ex1: Her CV highlighted collaboration, adaptability, and originality as core soft skills.
p2.ex2: Management assessed the collaboration skills of every employee during the review.
p2.example: Collaboration between the assistant and accountant prevented the business going bankrupt.

p2.en: To ask someone for advice or information.
p2.ex1: The assistant consulted the employee about the dress code before updating the CV.
p2.ex2: Management consulted each collaboration partner to assess the risk of going bankrupt.
p2.example: She consulted the accountant before assessing the management argument.

p2.en: A written summary of your education, qualifications, and work experience.
p2.ex1: The management team assessed every CV for relevant dress code and work experience.
p2.ex2: Her CV demonstrated the ability to run a business without facing rejection or going bankrupt.
p2.example: She updated her CV to highlight soft skills like collaboration, adaptability, and originality.

p2.en: A set of rules about what clothing is acceptable in a particular place.
p2.ex1: Assessing the dress code argument helped the assistant understand company soft skills.
p2.ex2: Collaboration between the accountant and management produced a clear dress code policy.
p2.example: The employee consulted management about the dress code before her first day.

p2.en: A person who is paid to work for an organisation.
p2.ex1: The accountant managed employee salaries to prevent the business going bankrupt.
p2.ex2: She became an employee after her CV demonstrated originality and management skills.
p2.example: Every employee was assessed for soft skills, adaptability, and collaboration.

p2.en: To be officially declared unable to pay your debts.
p2.ex1: The accountant assessed the finances and warned the employee about going bankrupt.
p2.ex2: She consulted the management team to avoid going bankrupt during the rejection period.
p2.example: Poor management and lack of collaboration caused the business to go bankrupt.

p2.en: To be in charge of something; or to succeed in doing something difficult.
p2.ex1: The employee managed the dress code policy after consulting management.
p2.ex2: Assessing soft skills helps management avoid going bankrupt when running a business.
p2.example: She managed the collaboration between the accountant and assistant efficiently.

p2.en: The process of controlling and organising an organisation or group.
p2.ex1: She assessed management alongside soft skills and adaptability in every CV.
p2.ex2: The assistant consulted management about the dress code and employee rejection process.
p2.example: Good management and collaboration prevent the business from going bankrupt.

p2.en: The ability to think or create in new and different ways.
p2.ex1: Her CV demonstrated originality in running a business and developing collaboration.
p2.ex2: Originality and soft skills are equally assessed during the employee recruitment process.
p2.example: The management team assessed originality and adaptability as key soft skills.

p2.en: The act of not accepting someone or something.
p2.ex1: The assistant consulted management about handling employee rejection professionally.
p2.ex2: Adaptability helps employees cope with rejection when running a business.
p2.example: She faced rejection after her CV was assessed as lacking soft skills and collaboration.

p2.en: To manage and operate a company or commercial enterprise.
p2.ex1: The accountant managed the finances so she could run the business without going bankrupt.
p2.ex2: Assessing your CV for originality and management skills is essential to run a business.
p2.example: She needed adaptability, collaboration, and strong soft skills to run a business.

p2.en: Personal qualities such as communication, teamwork, and adaptability that help you work well with others.
p2.ex1: Management assessed soft skills alongside the dress code and employee behaviour.
p2.ex2: To run a business, soft skills are as critical as technical accountant expertise.
p2.example: Her CV highlighted soft skills including collaboration, adaptability, and originality.

p2.en: The state of not having a job; the number of people without jobs.
p2.ex1: The accountant managed finances carefully to prevent employee unemployment.
p2.ex2: Adaptability reduces unemployment risk when running a business in difficult conditions.
p2.example: Unemployment forced her to assess her CV and develop new soft skills.

p3.en: A person whose job is making or repairing wooden objects and structures.
p3.ex1: Her profession as a carpenter required stability, lifting, and teamwork.
p3.ex2: The carpenter's salary was temporary but the profession offered long-term stability.
p3.example: The carpenter assessed the working environment before using heavy machinery.

p3.en: Not staying the same; changing in a way that is not predictable.
p3.ex1: The temporary salary was inconsistent, adding to the carpenter's insecurity.
p3.ex2: Irregular and inconsistent machinery maintenance increased work-related lifting risks.
p3.example: Inconsistent productivity in the working environment caused instability in the team.

p3.en: A feeling of uncertainty and anxiety about yourself or your situation.
p3.ex1: The carpenter's insecurity about irregular lifting tasks affected teamwork and productivity.
p3.ex2: Work-related insecurity increases when permanent stability in the profession declines.
p3.example: Temporary employment and inconsistent salary caused insecurity in the working environment.

p3.en: Something that stops an activity for a period of time.
p3.ex1: The carpenter faced an interruption from inconsistent lifting equipment in the profession.
p3.ex2: Temporary interruptions in salary and stability increased work-related insecurity.
p3.example: Irregular machinery interruptions reduced productivity and teamwork in the working environment.

p3.en: Not following a regular pattern; not consistent.
p3.ex1: The carpenter's salary was irregular and inconsistent, leading to work-related insecurity.
p3.ex2: Irregular machinery maintenance caused interruptions and reduced productivity.
p3.example: Irregular lifting tasks in the working environment caused insecurity and instability.

p3.en: The action of picking up or raising something heavy.
p3.ex1: Irregular lifting and inconsistent machinery increased work-related insecurity.
p3.ex2: The profession demanded lifting alongside teamwork, productivity, and stable working conditions.
p3.example: Heavy lifting in the carpenter's working environment required permanent stability.

p3.en: Machines or mechanical equipment used in industry or manufacturing.
p3.ex1: The carpenter assessed the working environment for safe lifting and machinery use.
p3.ex2: Work-related insecurity increased when inconsistent machinery caused instability.
p3.example: Irregular machinery maintenance caused interruptions and reduced productivity.

p3.en: Lasting or intended to last indefinitely.
p3.ex1: The carpenter sought a permanent working environment to reduce insecurity.
p3.ex2: Permanent employment provides stability and reduces work-related inconsistency.
p3.example: She left her temporary role for a permanent position offering salary stability.

p3.en: The efficiency with which work is done; how much output is produced.
p3.ex1: Teamwork and stability increased productivity in the carpenter's profession.
p3.ex2: Work-related interruptions and insecurity consistently lower productivity and morale.
p3.example: Irregular machinery and inconsistent lifting reduced productivity in the working environment.

p3.en: A paid job that requires specialised training or education.
p3.ex1: Her profession offered permanent stability despite inconsistent and irregular salary periods.
p3.ex2: Work-related insecurity in the profession increased during irregular machinery interruptions.
p3.example: Carpentry is a profession that requires lifting, teamwork, and machinery expertise.

p3.en: A fixed regular payment for employment, usually paid monthly.
p3.ex1: She sought a permanent profession with a stable and regular salary.
p3.ex2: Work-related insecurity increased when the irregular salary failed to reflect productivity.
p3.example: The temporary salary was inconsistent and caused insecurity in the working environment.

p3.en: The quality of being firm, steady, and not likely to change.
p3.ex1: The carpenter valued stability and teamwork over an inconsistent temporary profession.
p3.ex2: Permanent employment provides stability, productivity, and reduces irregular interruptions.
p3.example: Stability in salary and working environment reduced work-related insecurity.

p3.en: Not likely to change or fail; firmly established.
p3.ex1: She sought a stable profession with consistent machinery and regular lifting routines.
p3.ex2: Teamwork and productivity are stronger in a stable and permanent working environment.
p3.example: A stable salary and permanent working environment reduced the carpenter's insecurity.

p3.en: The ability to work cooperatively with others towards a shared goal.
p3.ex1: The carpenter's profession required stable teamwork and consistent productivity.
p3.ex2: Permanent stability increases teamwork and reduces work-related irregular interruptions.
p3.example: Teamwork in the working environment reduced machinery interruptions and insecurity.

p3.en: Lasting for only a limited time; not permanent.
p3.ex1: The carpenter took a temporary profession while seeking permanent working environment stability.
p3.ex2: Temporary lifting roles increased insecurity and reduced long-term productivity.
p3.example: Her temporary role lacked stability and offered an inconsistent, irregular salary.

p3.en: The conditions and surroundings in which work is carried out.
p3.ex1: The carpenter assessed the working environment for irregular lifting and machinery risks.
p3.ex2: Teamwork and productivity improve when the working environment is permanent and stable.
p3.example: A stable working environment with consistent machinery reduces insecurity and interruptions.

p3.en: Connected to or caused by your job or profession.
p3.ex1: The carpenter reported work-related interruptions from unstable machinery in the environment.
p3.ex2: Permanent stability reduces work-related insecurity and improves productivity.
p3.example: Work-related insecurity increased with irregular salary and inconsistent lifting demands.
